overview.text: The Ring-necked Snake is a small, harmless snake found across much of the United States and into Canada and Mexico. It is secretive, often hiding under logs and stones, and has a bright ring around its neck.

identification.text: Plain olive, brown, bluish-grey or nearly black on the back, with a bright yellow, red or orange ring around the neck. A few populations have no ring, and in some areas the ring is broken.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: South-eastern Canada, most of the United States and south into central Mexico.

habitat.text: Many habitats, wherever there is plenty of cover: open woodland near rocky hillsides, forests, damp places with fallen wood, and streamside areas in dry regions.

behaviour.text: Spends much of its time under cover or underground and is mostly active at night, so it is rarely seen by day.

diet.text: Mainly small salamanders, earthworms and slugs.

reproduction.text: Usually lays eggs; occasionally gives birth to live young.

recognise.text: Bright yellow, orange or red ring around the neck.
